# inference


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`Decider.predict(state, questions)` returns the Jev answer schema, so a
model trained with sysone drops into anything written for Jev or Laya.
It builds one row per question with the saved template and transforms,
batches them (padding to the longest, markers padded and masked), runs
one forward pass, divides each row’s logits by its bucket’s temperature,
and fills the schema. Several questions are several rows of one batch;
the cost grows with questions, never with a second pass.

### Decider

``` python
def Decider(
    model:sysone.models.EncoderDecisionModel, # encoder and head
    builder:sysone.template.RowBuilder, # the template and transforms of training
    temperatures:dict | None=None, # per type and option-count bucket
    device:NoneType=None, # where to run; the model stays where it is by default (`Decider.load` picks CUDA, MPS, CPU)
    dtype:NoneType=None, # autocast dtype; fp16 on CUDA, none (fp32) elsewhere
    batch_size:int=64, # rows per forward pass
    digits:int | None=4, # rounding of reported numbers, as Laya rounds
    name:str='sysone', # the model name reported by the HTTP API
    chunk:int | None=None, # score choices wider than this coarse to fine, in chunks of at most `chunk` options
    meta:dict | None=None, # the export's sysone.json, when loaded from one
    act_threshold:float | dict | None=None, # act where the act score ≥ this, per type and bucket (fitted by `learn.calibrate`)
    act_score:str='head', # the act score: the act head's p(act) ('head') or the calibrated top probability ('confidence')
):
```

*Typed answers from a decision model and the row builder it was trained
with*

### Answering

[`_rows`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/datasets.html#_rows)
runs the transforms once per state and builds the rows from the
transformed record, so a transform that changes a question, such as a
[`Shortlist`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/data.html#shortlist),
is seen by the answer too.
[`_scores`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/interpret.html#_scores)
runs the rows in chunks of `batch_size` and returns their logits and,
from a model with an act head, each row’s p(act) (`_logits` keeps only
the logits);
[`_probs`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/evaluate.html#_probs)
(and `_probs_record`, for a record already transformed) turns each row’s
logits into option probabilities at its bucket’s temperature; `_answer`
fills the schema.

### Wide option sets

Options share `head_max_len`, which is Laya’s known weakness above about
twenty options (0.425 on Banking77’s 77 intents). With `chunk=n` a wider
choice is scored coarse to fine, the pattern the laya-browser servers
use: its options are dealt into interleaved chunks of at most n, each
chunk is a row of a first pass, and the chunk winners meet in one row of
a second pass. An option’s probability is its chunk winner’s probability
in the final row times its own within its chunk, which sums to one over
all the options. The transforms run first, once, so a question is
chunked as they leave it (a
[`Shortlist`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/data.html#shortlist)
may have made it narrow enough already).

A learner answers from the model in memory, before any export:
`learn.decider()` wraps its model, builder and temperatures in a
[`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider),
and `learn.predict` is a shortcut.

``` python
rec = recs[1]
ans = learn.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"])
ans
```

Questions whose definitions cannot be answered fail with the question’s
name, as Laya’s runtime does:

``` python
jev = learn.decider()
test_fail(lambda: jev.predict("x", {"q": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Pick", "criteria": []}}), contains="'q'")
test_eq(jev.predict("x", {}), {})
```

Coarse to fine on a 40-option question with chunks of 8: five first-pass
rows and one final row, and the probabilities still sum to one:

``` python
wide_q = {"intent": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What does the customer want?", "criteria": [f"intent {i}" for i in range(40)]}}
wide_jev = learn.decider(chunk=8)
aw = wide_jev.predict("my card has not arrived yet", wide_q)["intent"]
test_eq((len(aw["probabilities"]), aw["chunks"]), (40, 5))
test_close(sum(aw["probabilities"].values()), 1.0, eps=1e-3)
test_eq(wide_jev.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]), jev.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]))   # narrow questions: unchanged
aw["choice"], aw["answer_confidence"]
```

## Export

`learn.export(path)` writes one folder that sysone and, when the
template allows, Laya can read:

    my-jev/
      sysone.json         template, transforms, head shape, temperatures, encoder reference, regime, metrics, training record
      environment.txt     every installed package, name==version
      head.safetensors    type embedding, head layers, scorer
      tokenizer/          (or processor/ for multimodal encoders)
      streams/<name>/     each side stream's tokenizer
      encoder/            the encoder's config, and its weights when they are bundled (a stream encoder: text/, sides/<name>/ and its own file)
      adapter/            the adapter, when it is kept (merge=False)
      rl_agent_config.json + model.safetensors   Laya's format, when the template is Laya's

- `sysone.json` also holds the [training record](05a_record.ipynb) under
  `training`: the commit, packages, hardware, data, settings and fits
  that made the model. `environment.txt` lists every installed package,
  to rebuild the environment from.
- Adapters are merged at export, so a LoRA or MiCA run ships as a plain
  encoder; `merge=False` keeps the adapter in `adapter/`, for further
  training or for a model that also works without it (the [diffusion
  model](24_mdlm.ipynb) writes with its base model). Over a Hub encoder
  whose own weights did not train, the adapter goes alone: the export
  names the encoder and the commit it trained on, megabytes instead of
  the encoder’s gigabytes, and
  [`Decider.load`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider.load)
  puts the adapter back on it. A local encoder, or one whose weights
  trained too, is bundled under the adapter.
- A head-only run on a Hub encoder stays small: the export holds the
  head and the encoder’s id and revision, and
  [`Decider.load`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider.load)
  pulls the encoder. `bundle=True` copies the weights in; a local
  encoder is always bundled.
- When the template, the head and the transforms are Laya’s,
  `laya="auto"` also writes `rl_agent_config.json` and a single
  `model.safetensors` with Laya’s parameter names, which `laya.Agent`,
  `laya[serve]` and `laya-mlx` load as they are. The encoder weights
  then live in that file only, and `encoder/` holds the config.

What decides the encoder’s part of an export:

``` {mermaid}
flowchart TB
    X["learn.export(path)"] --> AD{"adapters kept?<br/>(merge=False)"}
    AD -- yes --> BT{"a local encoder, or did its own<br/>weights train too?"}
    BT -- yes --> KEEP["encoder/: the weights under the adapter,<br/>and adapter/ beside them"]
    BT -- no --> ALONE["adapter/ alone, and the encoder's id<br/>at the commit it trained on<br/>(bundle=True copies the weights in)"]
    AD -- no --> T{"did the encoder train?<br/>(the regime is not head, or it trained before a freeze)"}
    T -- yes --> BUN["bundled: its weights are written"]
    T -- no --> LOC{"a local encoder?"}
    LOC -- yes --> BUN
    LOC -- no --> REF["the encoder's id and revision only<br/>(bundle=True copies the weights in)"]
    BUN --> LY{"Laya's template, head<br/>and no inference transforms?"}
    LY -- yes --> LF["rl_agent_config.json + model.safetensors:<br/>Laya's format, the adapters merged"]
    LY -- no --> ENC["encoder/: a plain encoder, the adapters merged"]
```

## Decider.load

`Decider.load(path)` reads a folder (or a Hub repo, with a subfolder
written `owner/repo/subfolder`) and picks the backend: a `sysone.json`
loads the sysone head over its encoder, a bare `rl_agent_config.json`
loads a Laya checkpoint as it is, and a GLiNER2 checkpoint loads the
GLiNER2 backend (`sysone.gliner`, which needs the `gliner2` package).
Backends register in `DECIDER_BACKENDS`. Underneath,
[`load_export`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#load_export)
rebuilds an export’s model (with the
[`EncoderSpec`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/models.html#encoderspec)
of its encoder), row builder and `sysone.json`;
[\[`load_learner`\](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#load_learner)](#load_learner)
builds on it too.

### Laya compatibility

The same folder loads in `laya.Agent`, Laya’s own runtime, which
rebuilds the rows with its own code and reads the temperatures from
`rl_agent_config.json`. Its answers match sysone’s on every fixture case
(Laya adds an `action` field, from an action head sysone does not train;
it is written as zeros, so Laya reports an action probability of 1):

``` python
import laya
```

``` python
agent = laya.Agent(str(out), device="cpu")
for rc in recs:
    ours, theirs = jev.predict(rc["state"], rc["questions"]), agent.predict(rc["state"], rc["questions"])["answers"]
    for qid in ours:
        a, b = ours[qid], theirs[qid]
        test_eq(a["type"], b["type"])
        for key in ("choice", "score", "noul", "confidence", "answer_confidence"):
            if key in a: test_close(a[key], b[key], eps=2e-4) if not isinstance(a[key], str) else test_eq(a[key], b[key])
        if "probabilities" in a: test_close(list(a["probabilities"].values()), list(b["probabilities"].values()), eps=2e-4)
theirs[qid]
```

<div>

> **Finding: an export after freezing dropped the trained encoder**
>
> The first export looked only at the current regime: after `unfreeze`,
> `fit` and `freeze`, the regime reads `head`, so it wrote the head and
> a reference to the Hub encoder, and the encoder the head had been
> trained on was lost. `_run` now marks the model when its encoder
> trains, and the export bundles the encoder whenever that mark is set.
> The same review found the dtype problem: a checkpoint stored in bf16
> was served in bf16 though its head was trained on float32 features;
> the export now records the dtype the encoder trained in, and the
> loader restores it.

</div>

An encoder that trained is exported even when the regime is back to
`head` (unfreeze, fit, freeze), since the head was trained on it; and
the export records the dtype the encoder trained in, which the loader
restores, rather than the dtype a checkpoint happens to be stored in:

``` python
torch.manual_seed(0)
lf = sysone.learner.decision_learner(data, FIX, train="head", preset="cpu", loss="soft_ce")
lf.unfreeze(); lf.fit(1, lr=1e-3); lf.freeze()
lf.model.spec.id = "someone/an-encoder-on-the-hub"          # as if it came from the Hub
outf = lf.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "refrozen", laya=False)
test_eq(json.loads((outf / "sysone.json").read_text())["encoder"]["weights"], "encoder")
test_eq(Decider.load(outf, device="cpu").predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]), lf.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]))

bf = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "bf16-encoder"
AutoModel.from_pretrained(FIX).to(torch.bfloat16).save_pretrained(bf); AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(FIX).save_pretrained(bf)
lb = sysone.learner.decision_learner(data, str(bf), train="head", preset="cpu", loss="soft_ce")
test_eq(next(lb.model.encoder.parameters()).dtype, torch.float32)
outb = lb.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "bf16", bundle=False, laya=False)
test_eq(json.loads((outb / "sysone.json").read_text())["encoder"]["dtype"], "float32")
test_eq(next(Decider.load(outb, device="cpu").model.encoder.parameters()).dtype, torch.float32)
```

A wide question whose options a transform thins out still answers, the
removed options at probability 0:

``` python
from sysone.template import Transform, transform
```

``` python
@transform("DropEven")
class DropEven(Transform):
    def __call__(self, record):   # drops "intent 0", "intent 2", ...: every option whose number is even, and says so
        keep = lambda c: int(str(c).split()[-1]) % 2 == 1
        qs = {q: {**d, "criteria": [c for c in d["criteria"] if keep(c)]} for q, d in record["questions"].items()}
        dropped = {q: [c for c in d["criteria"] if not keep(c)] for q, d in record["questions"].items()}
        return {**record, "questions": qs, "dropped": dropped}
thin = Decider(learn.model, RowBuilder(learn.data.builder.tok, learn.data.builder.template, [DropEven()]), chunk=4)
aw2 = thin.predict("my card has not arrived", wide_q)["intent"]
test_eq((len(aw2["probabilities"]), aw2["probabilities"]["intent 0"], aw2["shortlisted"], aw2["chunks"]), (40, 0.0, True, 5))
test_close(sum(aw2["probabilities"].values()), 1.0, eps=1e-3)
```

``` python
def probs(a): return list(a["probabilities"].values()) if "probabilities" in a else [a["noul"]]
a3 = Decider.load(out3, device="cpu").predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"])
b3 = ll.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"])
for qid in a3: test_close(probs(a3[qid]), probs(b3[qid]), eps=1e-3)
```

### Side streams and the act head in an export

An export of a model with side streams saves each stream’s tokenizer
under `streams/`, the stream encoder as transformers folders plus its
own small file, and the head’s whole shape: its readout, its query and
its act head. The act threshold fitted by `calibrate` goes into
`sysone.json`, and the loaded
[`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider)
reports `action` exactly as the learner’s did. On the fixture, a stream
of free-text notes stands in for a protein: the tiny ModernBERT reads
the row, a tiny ESM reads the notes, and a pair head scores the options
against the notes’ vector:

``` python
from transformers import AutoConfig, EsmConfig, EsmModel
```

``` python
def notes_spec():
    "A spec whose encoder is the fixture's text encoder beside a tiny ESM over a `notes` stream"
    tk = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(FIX)
    def loader(spec, dtype=torch.float32, **kw):
        torch.manual_seed(0)
        side = EsmModel(EsmConfig(vocab_size=len(tk), hidden_size=32, num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=2, intermediate_size=64,
                                  max_position_embeddings=64, pad_token_id=tk.pad_token_id, position_embedding_type="absolute",
                                  token_dropout=False), add_pooling_layer=False)
        special = (tk.cls_token_id, tk.sep_token_id, tk.pad_token_id)
        return StreamEncoder(AutoModel.from_pretrained(FIX, dtype=dtype), {"notes": SideEncoder(side, special)}).to(dtype)
    return EncoderSpec(FIX, AutoConfig.from_pretrained(FIX), tk, loader=loader, streams=[TokenStream("notes", tk, max_len=24)])

srecs = [dict(r, state={"text": json.dumps(r["state"]), "notes": f"note {i}: the customer wrote {i % 3} times"}) for i, r in enumerate(recs)]
sdata = TypedDecisions.from_records(srecs, valid=0.25, calib=0.25, tfms=[Stream("notes")])
torch.manual_seed(0)
slearn = sysone.learner.decision_learner(sdata, notes_spec(), train="head", preset="cpu", loss="soft_ce", head="pair",
                                         query="stream:notes", act=True, calibrate_after_fit=False)
slearn.fit(1, lr=1e-3); slearn.calibrate(act_accuracy=0.5)
sq = srecs[1]
before = slearn.predict(sq["state"], sq["questions"])
sout = slearn.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "notes-jev")
sjev = Decider.load(sout, device="cpu")
test_eq(sjev.predict(sq["state"], sq["questions"]), before)
test_eq(sorted(p.name for p in (sout / "streams").iterdir()), ["notes"])
test_eq((sout / "encoder" / "stream_encoder.json").exists(), True)
test_eq(sjev.act_threshold, slearn.act_threshold)
next(iter(before.values()))
```

## load_learner

[`Decider.load`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider.load)
gives a model’s answers; `load_learner(path, data)` gives its learner
back, to keep training, evaluate or interpret a model trained elsewhere
(on a Colab VM, a Kaggle kernel, a SageMaker job, or last week), as
fastai’s
[`load_learner`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#load_learner)
does. fastai pickles its
[`Learner`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/learner.html#learner);
sysone rebuilds one from the export instead:

- the model, from its weights
  ([`load_export`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#load_export)),
  with its encoder’s
  [`EncoderSpec`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/models.html#encoderspec)
  rebuilt from what the export holds, so the next export names the same
  encoder;
- the rows, from the template and transforms the model trained with,
  bound to `data` (data without transforms of its own takes the
  export’s);
- the regime it trained in, or another one (`train=`). An adapter the
  export kept comes back through
  [`set_regime`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/models.html#set_regime),
  as in a new learner, so `freeze` and `unfreeze` know its parameters,
  and then takes its weights. A LoRA merged into the encoder goes on
  with a new adapter of the same settings, which starts at zero: the
  answers are the export’s until it trains;
- its temperatures, act threshold, loss and learning rate.

An encoder that came in the export (anything but a Hub reference) is
marked as trained, so a later export bundles it again rather than
pointing at the Hub’s. And the learner keeps the export’s training
record as `resumed_from`, which its own exports write into theirs: the
record of a model trained further says what it continued.

<div>

> **Finding: a pickled model broke across transformers versions**
>
> Pickling, as fastai does, was tried first. The learner itself cannot
> be pickled: transformers’ `Trainer` inside it holds a weak reference.
> A pickled
> [`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider)
> saves, and loads back with the same answers once `torch.load` is given
> `weights_only=False` (since PyTorch 2.6 it refuses to unpickle
> arbitrary objects, which can run code). But under transformers 5.0,
> the version Kaggle runs, that pickle, made with 5.17, failed:
> `'ModernBertConfig' object has no attribute 'reference_compile'`. A
> pickle stores objects as one version of a library lays them out; an
> export stores weights and a configuration, and the same export loaded
> under both versions with the same answers. An export is also safe to
> load from the Hub, and a head-only model’s export holds the head, not
> a copy of the encoder.

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/inference.py#L349"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### load_learner

``` python
def load_learner(
    path, data:sysone.data.TypedDecisions, train:NoneType=None, lora:dict | None=None, subfolder:str | None=None,
    revision:str | None=None, **kw
)->sysone.learner.Learner:
```

*A
[`Learner`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/learner.html#learner)
on `data` from a sysone export (a folder or a Hub repo), to keep
training, evaluate or interpret it;
[`train`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/cli.html#train) changes
its regime*

Each kind of export comes back answering as it was exported. The full
fine-tune above, in Laya’s format, trains on:

``` python
fresh = lambda: TypedDecisions.from_json("fixtures/typed_decisions_tiny.jsonl", valid=0.25, calib=0.25)
rl = load_learner(out, fresh(), preset="cpu")
test_eq((rl.model.regime, rl.model.spec.id, rl.temperatures, rl.model.encoder_trained),
        (jev.model.regime, json.loads((out / "sysone.json").read_text())["encoder"]["id"], jev.temperatures, True))
for rc in recs[:6]: test_eq(rl.predict(rc["state"], rc["questions"], device="cpu"), jev.predict(rc["state"], rc["questions"]))
rl.fit(1, lr=1e-3)
```

An export that kept its adapter comes back with the same parameters
trainable, and finds them again after `freeze` and `unfreeze`; here with
MiCA, whose fixed matrices must stay fixed, and with the LoRA export
above:

``` python
trainable = lambda m: {n for n, p in m.encoder.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad}
torch.manual_seed(0)
lmc = sysone.learner.decision_learner(data, FIX, train="mica", preset="cpu", loss="soft_ce")
lmc.fit(1, lr=5e-3)
outm = lmc.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "mica", merge=False)
rlm = load_learner(outm, fresh(), preset="cpu")
test_eq((rlm.model.regime, trainable(rlm.model)), ("mica", trainable(lmc.model)))
rlm.freeze(); rlm.unfreeze()
test_eq(trainable(rlm.model), trainable(lmc.model))
am, bm = rlm.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"], device="cpu"), Decider.load(outm, device="cpu").predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"])
for qid in am: test_close(probs(am[qid]), probs(bm[qid]), eps=1e-3)
rl3 = load_learner(out3, fresh(), preset="cpu")
test_eq((rl3.model.regime, trainable(rl3.model)), ("lora", trainable(ll.model)))
```

Folding an adapter into the encoder changes the weights under the next
one, so that export must carry them; an adapter that came alone goes out
alone again:

``` python
rlx = load_learner(outm, fresh(), train="lora", preset="cpu")      # MiCA folded into the encoder, a new LoRA over it
test_eq(rlx.model.base_trained, True)
test_fail(lambda: rlx.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "x", merge=False, bundle=False), contains="must be exported")
rl4 = load_learner(out4, fresh(), preset="cpu")
test_eq((rl4.model.regime, rl4.model.base_trained), ("lora", False))
```

A head-only export can go on in another regime. A new LoRA adapter
starts at zero, so the answers stay the export’s until it trains:

``` python
rl2 = load_learner(out2, fresh(), train="lora", preset="cpu")
test_eq(rl2.model.regime, "lora")
test_eq(rl2.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"], device="cpu"), lh.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]))
```

Trained on and exported again, the encoder that came in the export is
bundled again (it is not the Hub’s), its id stays the one it started
from, and the new record names what it continued:

``` python
rlf = load_learner(outf, fresh(), preset="cpu")
rlf.fit(1, lr=1e-3)
outf2 = rlf.export(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "refrozen-more", laya=False)
mf = json.loads((outf2 / "sysone.json").read_text())
test_eq((mf["encoder"]["id"], mf["encoder"]["weights"]), ("someone/an-encoder-on-the-hub", "encoder"))
prev = mf["training"]["resumed_from"]
test_eq((prev["source"], len(prev["training"]["training"]["fits"]), len(mf["training"]["training"]["fits"])), ("refrozen", 1, 1))
```

Side streams and the act head come back too; and a Laya checkpoint,
which has no sysone record, is for
[`Decider.load`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider.load):

``` python
rls = load_learner(sout, TypedDecisions.from_records(srecs, valid=0.25, calib=0.25, tfms=[Stream("notes")]), preset="cpu", calibrate_after_fit=False)
test_eq((rls.predict(sq["state"], sq["questions"]), rls.act_threshold), (before, sjev.act_threshold))
test_fail(lambda: load_learner(laya_only, fresh()), contains="not a sysone export")
```

## Writing text

A decision model built on a generative model (the [masked diffusion
model](24_mdlm.ipynb)) can also write.
`sample(config, model, ids, **kw)` is the generic function that writes:
given token ids, with masks where text is wanted and `max_new_tokens`
more masks appended, it returns the ids with every mask filled. It
dispatches on the model’s config class, so each family brings its own
way of writing, a diffusion model’s unmasking or an autoregressive
model’s decoding, and a model that cannot write says so.

`Decider.generate(prompt)` writes an answer to a prompt in the model’s
chat format, and `Decider.fill(prompt, template)` writes only into the
slots of a fixed text, a JSON value say, leaving the rest as it is. A
slot is a fixed number of masks (`n`), and a diffusion model fills every
one of them, often writing on past its value into what the template says
next; so a slot’s text ends at its closing quote when the template
quotes it, and otherwise where the template’s next text begins (`stop`
sets another end). Both run the model’s encoder with its adapters
switched off unless asked (`adapter=True`): the adapter learned to
decide, and the base model is the one that learned to write.
[`adapters_off`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#adapters_off)
is that switch, peft’s `disable_adapter` when there are adapters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/sgaseretto/sysonelib/blob/main/sysone/inference.py#L450"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def fill(
    prompt, template:str, n:int=16, slot:str='{}', adapter:bool=False, system:str | None=None, stop:str | None=None,
    **kw
)->list:
```

*The texts the model writes into `template`’s slots (each `slot` becomes
`n` masks) after `prompt`, the rest of the template kept as it is; each
ends at `stop`, by default at its closing quote or where the template’s
next text begins*

``` python
def generate(
    prompt, max_new_tokens:int=64, adapter:bool=False, system:str | None=None, **kw
)->str:
```

*The text the model writes for `prompt` (a string or chat messages),
with its base model unless `adapter`*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### adapters_off

``` python
def adapters_off(
    model
):
```

*Run a model’s encoder without its peft adapters, as its base model (or
as it is, when it has none)*

``` python
wtok = learn.data.builder.tok
test_fail(lambda: learn.decider().generate("Hello"), contains="no sampler for a ModernBertConfig")
class _EchoConfig: "a writer's config: its sampler fills every mask with the first token of the row"
def _echo(config:_EchoConfig, model, ids, tokenizer=None, max_new_tokens:int=0, **kw):
    x = torch.cat([ids, torch.full((ids.shape[0], max_new_tokens), tokenizer.mask_token_id)], 1)
    return torch.where(x == tokenizer.mask_token_id, x[:, :1], x)
sample.register(_echo)
test_eq(sample(_EchoConfig(), None, torch.tensor([[5, wtok.mask_token_id]]), tokenizer=wtok, max_new_tokens=1).tolist(), [[5, 5, 5]])
methods(sample)
```

A slot is a fixed number of masks, and a diffusion model fills them all.
Asked for a JSON string, the [real model](24_mdlm.ipynb) wrote its value
and then more JSON,
`Gorillaz", "album": "first studio album", "genre":`, so a quoted slot
ends at its closing quote (an escaped quote doesn’t end it), and any
other at the template’s next text. A sampler that always writes such a
text shows it:

``` python
class _WriterConfig: "a writer's config: its sampler writes the same text into a row's masks, over and over"
def _writes(config:_WriterConfig, model, ids, tokenizer=None, max_new_tokens:int=0, **kw):
    said, x = tokenizer('Ada", "age": 36, "x', add_special_tokens=False).input_ids, ids.clone()
    at = (x[0] == tokenizer.mask_token_id).nonzero().flatten()
    x[0, at] = torch.tensor((said * len(at))[:len(at)])
    return x
sample.register(_writes)
class _Encoder: config = _WriterConfig()
class _Model: encoder = _Encoder()
class _Writer(Decider):
    "A decider over the writer alone"
    def __init__(self, builder): self.model, self.builder, self.device, self.dtype = _Model(), builder, torch.device("cpu"), None
w = _Writer(learn.data.builder)
test_eq((w.fill("Who?", '{"name": "{}"}', n=12), w.fill("Who?", '{"name": "{}"}', n=12, stop=",")), (["Ada"], ['Ada"']))
test_eq((_slot_end('{"text": "', '"}'), _slot_end("Name: ", "\nAge: "), _slot_end("I like ", "")), ('"', "\nAge: ", None))
test_eq((_cut('say \\"hi\\" now", "x', '"'), _cut("Ada\nAge: 36", "\nAge: "), _cut('"', '"')), ('say \\"hi\\" now', "Ada", ""))
```

## ONNX

For serving a text model on CPUs without PyTorch,
[`export_onnx`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#export_onnx)
writes an ordinary export plus `model.onnx`: the encoder and the head as
one graph that returns a score for every position. The gather at the
anchors and the softmax stay outside the graph, in numpy, so one graph
serves any number of options.
[`OnnxDecider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#onnxdecider)
runs it with onnxruntime (`sysone[onnx]`) and answers as the
[`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider)
does; it is a
[`Decider`](https://sgaseretto.github.io/sysonelib/inference.html#decider)
whose logits come from the graph.

``` {mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph ONNX["model.onnx (any batch, any length)"]
        I["input_ids,<br/>attention_mask, qtype"] --> E["encoder"] --> H["head layers<br/>and scorer"] --> S["a score for every<br/>position (batch, L)"]
    end
    S --> GA["numpy: the scores<br/>at marker_pos"] --> SM["softmax over<br/>the options"]
```

Keeping the gather outside the graph is what lets one exported graph
serve questions with any number of options: the graph never sees K.

``` python
ox, (out4 / "model.onnx").stat().st_size
```

## Serving

`serve_app(decider)` is the forty-line FastAPI app: `POST /v1/systemone`
takes the Jev request body (`state`, `questions`, an optional `model`)
and answers `{model, answers, usage}`, and `GET /health` reports the
model and device. SageMaker’s routes are there too, so the same app
serves a SageMaker endpoint: `GET /ping`, and `POST /invocations` with
one request body or a list of them. Malformed bodies get 400 and
unanswerable questions 422, as Laya’s server does, and so does any other
error in the request’s content (a field a transform needs, an unreadable
image). Images travel inline, as base64 data URLs: a path in
`state.image` would make the server open files of its own choosing on a
client’s behalf, so paths are refused unless `allow_image_paths=True`.
For Laya-format text exports, `laya[serve]` serves the same route; this
app covers what Laya’s runtimes cannot load (other templates, multimodal
encoders). `sysone serve my-jev` runs it (needs `sysone[serve]`).

### serve_app

``` python
def serve_app(
    decider:__main__.Decider, max_questions:int=64, allow_image_paths:bool=False
):
```

*A FastAPI app answering `POST /v1/systemone` and `GET /health` with
`decider`, and SageMaker’s `GET /ping` and `POST /invocations`*

``` python
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
```

``` python
client = TestClient(serve_app(jev))
r = client.post("/v1/systemone", json={"state": rec["state"], "questions": rec["questions"], "model": "jev-latest"})
test_eq(r.status_code, 200)
test_eq(r.json()["answers"], json.loads(json.dumps(jev.predict(rec["state"], rec["questions"]))))
test_eq(client.post("/v1/systemone", json={"state": "x", "questions": {"q": {"type": "rank", "instructions": "?"}}}).status_code, 422)
test_eq(client.post("/v1/systemone", content=b"not json").status_code, 400)
test_eq(client.post("/v1/systemone", json={"state": {"image": "/etc/passwd", "text": "x"}, "questions": rec["questions"]}).status_code, 422)
test_eq(client.get("/ping").status_code, 200)
r2 = client.post("/invocations", json=[{"state": rec["state"], "questions": rec["questions"]}] * 2)
test_eq([a["answers"] for a in r2.json()], [r.json()["answers"]] * 2)
client.get("/health").json(), r.json()["usage"]
```
